profile.headline: AI Senior Software Engineer at Asana
profile.geoLocationName: New York, New York, United States
profile.summary:
Software Engineer at Asana | UC Berkeley Computer Science and Statistics graduate

I am passionate about building tools that help humanity thrive by empowering them to engage more collaboratively and empathetically with each other. I aspire to use my skills in software engineering and data to create solutions to people's needs in an increasingly interconnected data-driven world. 

I collaborate closely with designers, product managers and fellow engineers to plan, implement and iterate on product features that follow best practices and deliver high value to users and stakeholders. I value fostering an environment that enables contributors to do their best work and promotes collaboration through sharing knowledge (mentorship), sharing responsibilities (trust), and sharing one's self (authenticity).

I have extensive experience implementing product features as well as prototyping in TypeScript+React, and I have worked across various technologies including Node, python, Express, Redux and GraphQL in building web applications.

positions.title: Software Engineer Technical Lead
positions.description:
• Led initiatives on Asana's AI team for delivering LLM-powered features including designing the data model for and productionizing Asana's flagship agentic AI Chat feature with experience in prompt engineering GPT/Claude and RAG strategies for retrieving relevant data from Asana's Work Graph 
• Technical lead for the Insights team responsible for developing Asana's dashboard feature that allows users to report on work across projects and view the data within charts
• Served as project lead with up to 10 eng contributors on app features including the launch of a new project overview page and an A/B test of a redesigned home page with customizable widgets that have driven increases in adoption metrics
• Spearheaded technical work on task lists including improving page performance and paying down technical debt from redesign and data model migration
• Designed and implemented critical UI features for successful launch of redesigned list and board views of projects that have driven increased collaboration and visitation among users
• Served as project lead while working closely with product and design for shipping key fast-follow features to address biggest pieces of user feedback following launch of redesigned list view
• Mentored intern and full-time engineers through facilitating on-boarding, integrating them into the team's workflow and highlighting growth opportunities
• Developed new materials and conducted sessions for on-boarding new engineers to React and Asana’s framework for building front-end views

projects.title: Pokemon Smartwatch App (Android)
projects.description:
• Worked on team of four to implement XML, Java activities, services, and database with UX centered design
• Designed and implemented front-end visual display using XML and Java while querying from database

The project comprises of an android application that runs on the mobile phone and android smartwatch. Users should run the app on their mobile phone as well as their smartwatch. Upon starting the app, the app will be able to detect when the user is physically near a pokemon. The phone will launch a notification on the watch allowing the user to choose to capture the Pokemon. The user can swipe between different types of pokeballs to use for capture. Different pokeballs can increase the probability of successful capture. When the user successfully captures the pokemon, the pokemon is stored onto the user's phone. The user can look at a list of all pokemon both owned and not owned. Unencountered pokemon have "​???"​ in place of all their information. When viewing a specific pokemon, the user has the options of renaming the pokemon, feeding the pokemon, and releasing the pokemon. After having fed a pokemon a sufficient amount of food, the pokemon will level up. At a high enough level, the pokemon will evolve into the next type. The user is also able to view their inventory and a map showing the locations of encountered pokemon. From the map, the user can tap on the pokemon's icon to directly navigate to the pokemon's page.
